title: The Tiny Team in Blood
subtitle: A friendly 3D micro-world
coreQuestion: Why can blood help the body work?
learningGoals: Know that blood is made of different parts.
Recognize red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma.
Understand that different blood parts have different jobs.
misconceptions: All blood cells do the same job.
White blood cells are bad germs.

hero.title: The Tiny Team in Blood
hero.lead: Blood is not just red water. Many tiny team members are working inside it.
hero.sceneExplanation: The main scene is a gentle blood vessel micro-world: red blood cells carry oxygen like small delivery carts, white blood cells are larger and fewer like guards, platelets are tiny repair helpers, and plasma flows like a river carrying everyone along.
hero.childPrompt: Tap each tiny member and see what job it does in the body.
hero.parentPrompt: This page uses the ‘working team’ metaphor to explain blood components without scary or bloody visuals.

classificationGroups.name: Red blood cells
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Like little oxygen delivery carts that bring oxygen around the body.
classificationGroups.parentNote: At this age, focus on oxygen transport. Hemoglobin can be mentioned briefly.
classificationGroups.misconception: Red blood cells are not germs or ordinary red drops.

classificationGroups.name: White blood cells
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Like body guards that help protect you from invaders.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Do not expand into immune cell subtypes yet.
classificationGroups.misconception: White blood cells are helpers, not bad things.

classificationGroups.name: Platelets
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Like tiny repair helpers that help small wounds stop bleeding.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Explain clotting as a repair process without technical detail.
classificationGroups.misconception: Stopping bleeding is a process, not instant magic.

classificationGroups.name: Plasma
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Like the flowing river in blood that carries many things along.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Plasma is the liquid part of blood and transports many substances.
classificationGroups.misconception: Blood is not only cells; it also has a liquid part.

representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking the white cell is an invader.

representativeObjects.childExplanation: I carry the team as blood flows.

mechanism.title: How does oxygen travel through the body?

steps.childExplanation: When we breathe in, oxygen comes into the lungs.
steps.parentNote: No need to explain alveoli in detail.

steps.childExplanation: Red blood cells carry oxygen and get ready to travel.
steps.parentNote: You may mention hemoglobin as the helper inside red cells.

steps.childExplanation: The heart works like a pump that moves blood through the body.
steps.parentNote: The pump metaphor is enough for this page.

steps.childExplanation: Red cells bring oxygen to places that need to work.
steps.parentNote: Examples: muscles, brain, hands, and feet.

steps.childExplanation: Blood also carries waste gas back to be breathed out.
steps.parentNote: Call it carbon dioxide or waste gas.

secondaryMechanism.title: How do platelets help a small wound?

steps.childExplanation: When the skin has a small cut, the body needs a repair team.
steps.parentNote: Keep the visual soft and non-bloody.

steps.childExplanation: Platelets come together near the opening.
steps.parentNote: This is a simplified explanation of clotting.

steps.childExplanation: They help make a patch so bleeding can slow down.
steps.parentNote: Do not overpromise; serious wounds need adult help.

parentTips: Keep the tone gentle; avoid scary medical visuals.
Ask the child to match each cell to a job instead of memorizing names only.
This page can connect to immunity, heart, lungs, and wound healing.
acceptanceCriteria: The child can name at least two blood members.
The child can explain one job of red blood cells and one job of white blood cells.
The page does not create fear of blood or the body.
